column4: when a donor carries two variants of one type (immutablepool/Uuid128 174 lines, uuid/Uuid128 120 lines, committed 120 s apart on 2026-09-23), the brief's rule "newer by commit date" (uuid variant, 12:02:25 vs 12:00:25) conflicts with the byte-for-byte law: the dependent owners (Uuid128HashIndex, Uuid128Vector, UuidStorageFootprint) and the oracle bind to the older variant's API. The compile-closure pick wins, the rule and the loser's blob/commit/time go into an NEC row, and the loser's own oracle is replayed on the survivor through REWRITE rows (its method names mapped), which turns the pick into evidence instead of an opinion

column4: a reflective dump must never print an object's default toString: it carries the type name and an identity hash, both differ between donor and relocated runs. Records go through accessors (packed(), name(), canonical text), unknown objects print "<object>". The first run differed on exactly one line: the cancellation probe built an index over an EMPTY vector and the donor checks cancellation only per element, so no exception was thrown and the index object was printed; the probe now uses a one-element vector (CancellationException on both sides) and keeps the empty case as a documented non-cancellation
